assessments.reasoning: Wirth and Weber are named on the dated Stanford report. Chapter IV describes EULER as the algorithmic language whose syntax and semantics it defines, with the extension and generalization of ALGOL 60 explicit. The appendix names an EULER IV translator under a separate implementation heading.

challenge.method: Compare the Stanford title page, Chapter IV description, both errata sheets and the EULER IV appendix with the catalog’s implementation and machine entries. Reacquire a second archive copy to test scan identity.
challenge.results: The report defines a named algorithmic language as a conceptual generalization of ALGOL 60. The appendix concerns one translator system. Byte-identical copies are mirrors of one original report. Stanford direct access timed out.

limitations: The CHM machine list supplies scope controls. The record makes no compatibility or cross-implementation equivalence claim.
